handbookNote: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual (Supplement to the Nebraska Driver's Manual; base AAMVA '2005 CDL Testing System'/Modernized Testing System content, base Version: September 9, 2022 for Sections 1-2 and July 2017 for most other sections, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection and Section 12 Basic Control Skills modernized to Version: March 2025, cover page states Version: March 2025 (March 2026)), published by the Nebraska Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) -- fetched directly from https://dmv.nebraska.gov/sites/default/files/doc/Nebraska%20MOD%20CDL%20Driver's%20Manual%20-%20March%202026.pdf on 2026-08-22 (7.2MB PDF, full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/ne_cdl_research/ne_cdl_manual_full.txt, 9,963 lines, cross-checked against a pdftotext -raw extraction (ne_cdl_manual_raw.txt) for two-column sections). Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Exam mechanics: Nebraska's own manual (including its 11-page 'Nebraska Specifics' front-matter insert covering CDL/CLP applications, classes, endorsements, restrictions, CLP/CDL testing tables, ELDT, brake-check procedures, medical self-certification, security threat assessment, RCDL, third-party testers, and military waivers) does NOT disclose a specific per-test item count or numeric passing-score percentage anywhere in the fetched text -- this is a genuine gap in the official source, not an oversight, consistent with several other states built in this project (e.g. Alabama, Arkansas, Kansas, Indiana, Maine, Maryland, Minnesota, Mississippi). The federally standardized minimum passing score of 80 percent applies regardless (49 CFR 383.135(a)). Third-party CDL test-prep sites (e.g. epermittest.com, driving-tests.org, cdlpracticetest.com) converge on a General Knowledge test of 50 questions requiring 40 correct (80%) to pass, consistent with the common AAMVA-battery default, but this is NOT confirmed by Nebraska's own official manual and is cited here only as third-party corroboration, not as a verified official figure -- treat all item counts as unconfirmed/hedged in this track's exam-mechanics copy. Nebraska's three CDL vehicle classes are A (combination, GCWR 26,001+ lbs with towed unit over 10,000 lbs GVWR), B (single vehicle or combination with towed unit 10,000 lbs GVWR or less, GVWR 26,001+ lbs), and C (vehicle not meeting A/B, but placarded for hazardous materials or designed to carry 16+ passengers including the driver). Nebraska's six CDL endorsements are H (Hazardous Materials), N (Tank Vehicle), P (Passenger), S (School Bus), T (Double/Triple Trailers), and X (Combination Tank Vehicle and Hazardous Materials); CLP endorsements are limited to P, S, and N. Nebraska's CDL restriction codes are E, I, K, L, M, N, O, V, and Z (no separate 'no full air brake' code beyond Z). Minimum age is 21 for interstate or 18 for intrastate operation, Class A/B/C alike. A CLP is valid for one year and must be held at least 14 days before CDL skills testing; skills tests (vehicle inspection, basic control skills, on-road driving, taken strictly in that order) are administered by appointment only, and failing or not completing all three segments before CLP expiration invalidates any already-passed segments. ELDT (Entry Level Driver Training, effective February 7, 2022) is required before a first-time Class A or B CDL, a Class B-to-A upgrade, or a first-time P/S/H endorsement; the Nebraska DMV verifies ELDT completion via the federal Training Provider Registry (TPR) rather than administering training itself. Nebraska offers a Restricted CDL (RCDL) for seasonal farm/ranch-related service operators (Class B/C only, up to 210 days per 12-month period) and a military skills-test waiver (written tests still required). Hazardous Materials endorsement requires a TSA security threat assessment (fingerprint-based background check) handled by a third-party TSA agent, not the DMV; the CDL expires when the threat assessment expires. Content-depth rationale: Nebraska uses the same AAMVA-authored Modernized Testing System base manual as several other recently built CDL-track states in this project (e.g. Kentucky, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Missouri), organized into the same 13 core sections -- Section 1 Introduction (CDL classes, endorsements/restrictions, disqualifications, knowledge/skills test structure), Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section, split here into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering vehicle inspection, basic control, shifting, seeing/mirrors, communicating, distracted/aggressive driving, night driving and fatigue, fog, winter and hot-weather driving, railroad crossings, and mountain driving; 03_driving_safely_b covering driving emergencies, antilock braking systems, skid control/recovery, accident procedures, fires, alcohol/drugs, and hazardous materials rules for all commercial drivers), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (split into two buckets, 10_hazmat_a covering the intent of the regulations/shipper-carrier responsibilities/communication rules/placarding and 11_hazmat_b covering loading-unloading, driving/parking rules, emergencies, and the glossary), Section 10 School Buses, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection (Nebraska's modernized version, revised March 2025), Section 12 Basic Control Skills Test, and Section 13 On-Road Driving (12 and 13 combined into one bucket), plus Nebraska-specific administrative detail from the 11-page front-matter insert layered into the licensing bucket. Some sections (Transporting Cargo Safely, Transporting Passengers Safely, Doubles and Triples, Tank Vehicles) are naturally short in this manual and their question buckets were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Nebraska manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers.
